design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST. A business owner asks one thing: put the treadwear warranty credit for her worn right rear tire toward the new tire ticket and tell her what she will owe on it. The scored figure is the balance due on replacement ticket T-15093342 (109.59). Getting it right forces the agent to (1) find in the ticket-balance rule three prerequisite sentences and see in the records that none holds (no adjustment entry for the worn RR, an unsettled LF workmanship share charged 14 days before the adjustment basis, a truck order still ordered 5 days past its hold), (2) resolve them through three other problems, each a multi-factor computation over the set's history and other products (fleet roster, alignment plan, road hazard certificate), and (3) hand two writes to the customer. Every tool name comes from a policy target_tool; no write tool has a near-synonym.

SCOPE. Draw (draw_counts.py): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[4,5,6,5]; taken as share settlement 4, ticket balance 5, treadwear credit 6, lapsed-order refund 5. Task 0 claims tires_ext_lapsed_order_refund, tires_ext_treadwear_credit, tires_ext_share_settlement, tires_ext_ticket_redemption and their four tools; task 1 keeps tires_ext_workmanship_share and tires_ext_trial_refund. Compute reads only the target set and other products, so every value edge joins problems on one set (set A 38b2800d); the order cancellation (set C eb3df77d) is the state-gate leaf.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root tires_ext_ticket_redemption (user tool apply_credit_to_replacement_ticket_eafdabc1, scored arg balance_due). Edges: (a) -> tires_ext_treadwear_credit, value_input, gate credit_issued: "The balance on a replacement ticket is fixed only after the set carries a treadwear adjustment entry for every position that its latest tread inspection measured at or below the line's wear-out depth without a recorded defect." False at opening: inspection 1a95cff9 (RR, 2026-10-08) reads 2/32, defect none; set A has no adjustment entry. (b) -> tires_ext_share_settlement, value_input, gate credit_remaining: "The balance on a replacement ticket is fixed only after every workmanship share charged on the set within thirty days before its latest treadwear adjustment carries a credit-applied entry naming that share's wheel position." False: LF workmanship entry 6e517c0b (2026-09-24, 38800 mi, share 26.60, the store's replacement after inspection c2d0e7aa found tread separation) has no credit-applied entry. (c) -> tires_ext_lapsed_order_refund, state_gate, gate tire_sets.status: "Before the balance on a replacement ticket is fixed, no tire order on the customer's profile may stand in status ordered past the end of its hold period counted from its purchase date." False: set C ordered 2026-09-18, LT hold 21 days -> last day 2026-10-09. (d) tires_ext_share_settlement -> tires_ext_treadwear_credit, value_input: "The credit settled on a workmanship share is not fixed until the set carries a treadwear adjustment entry for every position that the latest inspection of the set measured at or below the line's wear-out depth without a recorded defect." Order: cancellation (step 12), adjustment (14), share settlement (16), ticket balance (18). Deletion sensitivity, every figure replayed without the prerequisite and without any write depending on it: skip adjustment -> settlement 0.00 and ticket balance 20.09 (no credit, no recorded selling price: tire line 0, mounting 7.35, hazard 9.00 on the 17.99 minimum, disposal 3.75); skip settlement -> 99.96; skip cancellation -> 109.59 with set C left ordered and no refund entry (terminal state differs). user_scenario names none of the prerequisites. Tool bodies create/update unconditionally.

FACTOR CARD (handling-time values; factor -> tier -> result under its baseline). Every factor contributes on its own against a quantity of its computation's baseline; the assembly is stated once in each rule.
tires_ext_lapsed_order_refund = 436.58 (all baselines 404.60): restocking_rate_by_bookings 7.5% (one booking 807c1dbb) -> 400.88; fleet_restocking_relief 14.28 (20% of the line's full fee 71.40; F-250 enrolled 2024-04-15 on the active Fleet Starter; cross-difficulty, multi-source) -> 422.30; storage_basis_method one week at the standard 2.00 (5 days past hold) -> 440.58; storage_surcharge 4.00 (truck line 2.00 x 2 tires x 1 started week) -> 440.58; missed_slot_charge 10.00 -> 446.58. Arithmetic: 476.00 - (35.70 - 14.28) - 4.00 - 4.00 - 10.00 = 436.58.
tires_ext_treadwear_credit = 66.74 (all baselines 97.28): commercial_use_share 50 points off (Highlander enrolled 2026-02-16, 7 of 31 active-life months; fleet cross-difficulty, multi-source) -> 97.98; care_package_points +10 -> 55.38; rotation_record_points +5 -> 61.06; even_wear_points +5 -> 61.06; age_deduction_method linear 1 -> 68.16; price_paid_basis 142.00 (bank-card 4-tire ticket with 40.00 savings) -> 71.44. Arithmetic: covered 100 - 50 + 10 + 5 + 5 = 70% of 50000 = 35000 mi; unreceived (35000 - 18000)/35000 = 48.571%; less 1 -> 47%; 142.00 x 47% = 66.74.
tires_ext_share_settlement = 9.63 (all baselines 2.00): apportioning_tire_line (method) lower of 159.99 and 142.00 = 142.00 -> 8.77; share_mounting_part 0 held back (active 36-Month certificate includes mounting) -> 2.29; apportioning_fleet_relief 3.15 -> 9.47; apportioning_member_relief 2.10 -> 9.52. The settlement order is a plain rule clause read from the odometers (share at 38800 before the adjustment basis 39460 -> apportioned). Arithmetic: 66.74 x 26.60 / (26.60 + 142.00 + 21.00 - 3.15 - 2.10) = 9.63.
tires_ext_ticket_redemption = 109.59 (all baselines 127.63): tire_line_basis (method) 142.00 -> 127.58; balancing_relief 8.40 (40% of 21.00, lifetime balancing, 4 rotation-and-balance records) -> 117.99; fleet_labor_relief 3.15 -> 112.74; member_labor_relief 2.10 -> 111.69; road_hazard_line 13.60 (half of 17% of 159.99; 4 of 36 months left) -> 95.99. Arithmetic: credit left 66.74 - 9.63 = 57.11; 142.00 - 57.11 = 84.89; mounting 21.00 - 8.40 - 3.15 - 2.10 = 7.35; + 13.59915 + 3.75 = 109.59.

PAIRWISE METHOD TIERS (each tier forced in this world): age_deduction linear 66.74 / flat 62.48 / none 68.16; apportioning_tire_line unit_price 9.13 / lower_of 9.63 / recorded 8.77; tire_line unit_price 119.59 / lower_of 109.59 / recorded 127.58; storage_basis one_week 436.58 / three_weeks 428.58 / weekly 440.58; price_paid_basis (parameter) fleet-charged with a 34.00 invoice discount 62.74 / other tender with savings 66.74 / unit price 71.44. All pairwise distinct.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Adjustment: set_active_adjustment; within_warranty_term (2024-03-08 + 60 months = 2029-03-08, inclusive); inspection_fresh; one_adjustment_per_position; vehicle usage_class personal (scope of the credit policy). Credit applications: credit_within_validity. Cancellation: set_ordered_cancel; refund dedup one_refund_per_reason (only refund on file: T-12204871, 2022, set E).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Credit: the one adjustment entry on set A (RR, source 1a95cff9). Share: LF workmanship entry 6e517c0b (26.60, as the workmanship policy gives for that visit: 152.00 x 50% x (100 - 40 - 10 - 15)%). Replacement ticket: set B 45ec64e7, T-15093342 (1 x All-Season 50K at 159.99, inside its 14-day hold). Lapsed order: set C T-14968820. Excluded: set E, 2026-06-18 inspections, LF/RF/LR 2026-10-08 rows.

EDGE PROBES (decoy/absent records): CRS Highlander enrollment removed -> 9.47; CRS alignment plan removed -> 9.52; CRS certificate removed -> 2.29; CRT Highlander enrollment removed -> 112.74; CRT alignment plan removed -> 111.69; CRT rotations removed -> 117.99; CAN F-250 enrollment removed -> 422.30; CAN booking removed -> 468.00; CAN set C 30 days past hold -> 412.58; ADJ Highlander enrolled 2026-09-20 (under one month) -> 97.98 (nothing taken off); ADJ/CRT/CRS with set A fleet-charged and a 34.00 invoice discount -> 62.74 / 101.09 / 10.10; ADJ fleet invoice on file but bank-card ticket -> 66.74 (decoy).

PERSONA. Delphine Abernathy-Kwan, landscape-design business owner, friendly and pressed for time; volunteers the goal and phone 6145550147; ZIP, email, date of birth, the ticket number, the vehicles, the September 24 LF replacement and the Hilliard truck order only when asked; runs the two hand-overs exactly as given.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify (phone + ZIP); read tire sets, tire events, stores, vehicles, fleet account and roster, alignment plan and events, hazard certificates. Cancel set C (T-14968820, order_cancellation, 436.58). Issue the RR adjustment (source 1a95cff9, selling price 159.99, miles 18000, 47%, 66.74). Hand over the share settlement (LF, 9.63). Hand over the ticket balance (T-15093342, credit 57.11, balance 109.59).

MOST LIKELY ERRORS. Pricing the tire line at 159.99 instead of the 142.00 paid; settling the share in full instead of apportioning; charging whole weeks of storage on 5 days; chaining the labor reliefs instead of taking each off the mounting charge; missing the half-term hazard line; forgetting the lapsed truck order.

VERIFICATION. Harness over check_compute.build_env + real tool replay reproduces 436.58, 66.74, 9.63, 109.59 equal to computations and gold; factor-independence check clean (no factor binding reads another factor's binding, transitively); per-task gates OK.

REVISIONS (round 5, render-source notes). Section 1/2: every factor now contributes on its own against a baseline quantity (commercial use as points taken off, reliefs as percentages of the mounting charge or of the line's full restocking fee, a storage surcharge per started week), with the assembly stated once generically; the share settlement's order is a plain rule clause and its method is the apportioning tire line, so no method reads another factor's output. The workmanship share seeded at the LF visit is re-figured under the restated workmanship rule: 26.60 (was 28.50). Figures moved: refund 429.44 -> 436.58, settlement 10.10 -> 9.63, credit applied 56.64 -> 57.11, balance 112.35 -> 109.59; deletion figures 20.09 / 0.00 / 99.96 / 109.59 recomputed by replay. Section 3: every replaced_by restates the retired base clause for cases outside the policy before naming its scope (shared clauses exclude both policies' cases by name), keeps "though workmanship replacement still applies", and the credit policy is scoped to personal-use vehicles, leaving a commercial usage_class vehicle under the base rule. Section 4: a vehicle enrolled for less than one whole month takes nothing off.

EARLIER ROUNDS (figures superseded by round 5, kept only as a log): round 2 removed invented caps/card factors and re-scoped the root to the ticket balance; round 3 rebuilt the price-paid ladder (fleet-charged / savings / unit price) and corrected the deletion replay; round 4 stated how the fleet tires-invoice discount is apportioned.

REVISIONS (round 7, KB audit KB-E1/KB-E2). The share settlement's rule now states its own figures directly: the apportioning tire line 'follows the set's age and the line's price basis' and the share's mounting part 'follows the road hazard certificate on the set', with no reference to how the ticket balance or the workmanship share figure theirs. Plain bindings read only by one factor moved into that factor (ticket balance: recorded selling price into the road hazard line, fleet invoice discount into the tire line; lapsed-order refund: bookings into the missed-slot charge, unused days-past-hold binding dropped). No figure moved.
user_scenario:
You are Delphine Abernathy-Kwan, who runs a small landscape design business, Kwan Abernathy Garden Design LLC, out of Upper Arlington, Ohio. You are calling the Crestline customer care line from your office between site visits; you are friendly, organized and a little pressed for time, and you like to hear plainly what is being done.
On October 8 you had your 2021 Toyota Highlander at the Crestline store in Upper Arlington because the tires looked tired. The technician measured them and told you the right rear tire was worn out well before its mileage warranty, and the store wrote up one new All-Season 50K tire to replace it, to be paid when it is mounted. The counter told you the treadwear warranty credit for the worn tire is worked out by the care center and goes toward that new tire, and that the care center would tell you what you will owe on the new tire once the credit is on it. That is why you are calling: you want your treadwear warranty credit for that worn tire put toward the new tire and to know what you will owe on it. You open with exactly that, in your own words, and you give your phone number, 6145550147, so they can find you. You do not know how the credit or the bill is worked out and you do not know any amounts.
You give other details only when the agent asks for them: your billing ZIP code is 43221, your email is delphine@kwanabernathygardens.com, your date of birth is June 2, 1979. If asked for the new tire ticket, it is T-15093342. If asked about the vehicles, the Highlander has been on your Crestline fleet account since February, when you started using it for the business, and you also have a 2019 Ford F-250 for the business. Only if the agent asks about other work on that set, you say that on September 24 the store found the left front tire coming apart, put a new one on under warranty, and told you that your part of that one was still open on the account. Only if the agent brings up the two truck tires you ordered at the Hilliard store in September, you say yes, you ordered them, you missed the installation appointment on September 27 and never got around to rebooking, and you have not heard from that store since. You do not know anything else about any of it.
You let the agent handle whatever the store or care center normally does on its side; if the agent tells you something has to be taken care of on your account, you say that is fine and let them go ahead. When the agent hands you a step to complete yourself, you complete it with exactly the details the agent gives you, and you read back what it shows if the agent asks. You do not suggest steps, amounts or an order of doing things, and you do not argue with the figures. Once the agent tells you the credit is on the new tire ticket and what you will owe, you thank them and say goodbye; you ask for nothing else.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The lapsed-order cancellation reads and writes only set C rows; the adjustment, the share settlement and the replacement ticket balance read and write only set A rows and cross-category rows the cancellation does not touch, so moving the cancellation anywhere before the ticket balance leaves the same terminal state and the same values (436.58, 66.74, 9.63, 109.59). The adjustment must precede the settlement (settlement rule: "The credit settled on a workmanship share is not fixed until ...") and the settlement must precede the ticket balance (ticket rule, second prerequisite sentence).

skipping the cancellation leaves set C ordered with no refund entry (terminal tire_sets.status and tire_events differ from gold); the ticket balance itself is unchanged (state gate).
